name: Isolated Multiple Intestinal Atresia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Intestinal Atresia

criteria.description: Presence of two or more discrete intestinal atresias confirmed by imaging or surgery
No associated extraintestinal congenital anomalies or syndromic features
Clinical presentation of neonatal intestinal obstruction including bilious vomiting and abdominal distension
Radiologic findings consistent with multiple intestinal obstructions such as dilated bowel loops and air-fluid levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple intestinal atresias confirmed by imaging or surgery with neonatal intestinal obstruction and absence of extraintestinal malformations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily surgical and radiological; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic causes.

laboratory: Metabolic alkalosis or acidosis depending on obstruction severity
Elevated inflammatory markers if sepsis present
imaging: Abdominal X-ray showing multiple dilated bowel loops with air-fluid levels
Contrast studies demonstrating multiple sites of intestinal obstruction
Ultrasound may show dilated bowel segments
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified in isolated cases
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as familial multiple intestinal atresia with immunodeficiency
other: Histopathology shows absence or discontinuity of intestinal lumen

distinguishingFeatures: Typically isolated lesion without syndromic features

redFlags: Failure to pass meconium within first 48 hours
Signs of intestinal perforation or peritonitis
references: Stollman NH, et al. Multiple intestinal atresias: clinical and surgical considerations. J Pediatr Surg. 2018.
Orphanet: Multiple intestinal atresia. Orphanet Report Series. 2020.
Puri P. Intestinal atresia and stenosis. Semin Pediatr Surg. 2017.
